subject: GPU headroom exhaustion — customer update & next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@zephyrai.com>, ops@zephyrai.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU headroom exhaustion — short incident note and immediate mitigation

Hi Sarah / Zephyr ops team,

Wanted to reach out with a brief update after we observed higher-than-expected contention on your Dedicated pool earlier this morning. Impact summary: some requests to your reserved cluster saw elevated queue times between 08:42–09:03 PDT; latency spikes were observed for tail requests under synth heavy loads. We briefly throttled new allocations to protect running sessions.

What we did immediately:
- Activated an emergency autoscale burst to adjacent capacity zones to reduce queuing.
- Applied a conservative prefix-KV cache preference to reduce repeated KV reads.
- Scoped the routing policy to route low-priority background jobs to best-effort nodes.

Current status: cluster is stable and serving; we are monitoring. Engineering is collecting logs and a GPU utilization snapshot. We plan to follow up with a concise root-cause note and recommended mitigations within the next 24 hours.

Attachments: autoscale-logs-0528.zip (log archive), gpu-snapshot-0528.png (utilization heatmap).

Immediate ask: please let us know if you saw any customer-facing errors or timeouts on your side so we can correlate.

Sorry for the disruption — we’ll own the follow-up and remediation path.

— Lauren

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU headroom exhaustion — short incident note and immediate mitigation

Lauren / team — quick internal notes (cc’d for context):

Preliminary findings:
- Root trigger: a workload shift from a partner test tenant caused sustained KV cache misses and serialization of KV loads on a subset of nodes leading to reduced headroom (per-GPU async queue growth).
- Autoscaler response was correct but the burst policy throttled allocation before warm pools were fully populated, which caused a short period of elevated queuing while new instances booted.

Immediate remediation applied:
- Increased warm pool target by 20% for the Zephyr pool to avoid cold-start queuing.
- Adjusted autoscale burst threshold to allow faster parallel allocations for this tenancy.
- Increased aggressive KV-proxy caching on the affected model endpoints.

Artifacts attached: autoscale-logs-0528.zip (scheduler traces), gpu-snapshot-0528.png (node heatmap). I’ll follow up with a short timeline and a draft postmortem for customer review.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@zephyrai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, ops@zephyrai.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident update: headroom exhaustion & our remediation plan

Hi Sarah / Zephyr ops,

Following up with the agreed customer-facing summary and next steps. Thanks for flagging the timeouts — that helped us correlate scheduler traces with your error windows.

Summary (what happened):
- Between 08:42–09:03 PDT on 2026-05-28, a partner-originated workload caused sustained KV cache churn on a subset of Zephyr’s Dedicated GPUs. This reduced available headroom and increased per-request queuing, producing the error spike you saw.

Immediate impact and actions taken (what we did):
- Burst allocation invoked; additional capacity came online but there was a short warm-up delay.
- We temporarily rerouted background jobs to best-effort capacity and tightened KV caching on affected endpoints.
- Warm pool targets increased by 20% for your pool to reduce future cold allocation windows.

Short-term mitigation plan (next 7 days):
- Keep increased warm pool and adjusted autoscale thresholds in place.
- Run a targeted soak test on your pool during low-traffic windows (we propose May 31, 03:00–04:00 PDT) to validate headroom behavior.
- Provide you with a filtered log bundle and a trace mapping for the error window (support ticket RED-78924).

Longer-term hardening (30–90 days):
- Implement autoscaler tuning that biases rapid warm allocation for pinned Dedicated pools.
- Add KV miss-rate alerts and a predictive headroom estimator to the Console for customers with reserved capacity.
- Offer an onboarding checklist to help signal partner test workloads that might affect headroom.

Attached: postmortem-draft-0529.pdf (concise one-page postmortem), autoscale-logs-0528.zip, gpu-snapshot-0528.png.

Requested next steps for Zephyr:
1) Confirm the proposed soak test window or suggest an alternative.
2) Share any additional traces or customer reports from your side for the 08:42–09:03 window.

We’re treating this as high priority and will keep you updated on follow-through items. If you’d like a short call to run through the plan and timeline, I’m happy to schedule.

Best,
Lauren
